newsitem.title: USA: First Union sees Signet adding to earnings.
newsitem.headline: First Union sees Signet adding to earnings.

text.p: First Union Corp vice chairman John Georgius told an interviewer on CNBC Monday that he expects the company's planned acquisition of Signet Banking Corp to add $0.13 per share to 1999 earnings.

Earlier Monday, First Union said in a news release that the merger will have a positive impact on 1998 earnings and be increasingly positive afterward. The release did not give any figures for earnings accretion.
Then $3.25 billion stock transaction is expected to close by December 31.
Asked about possible antitrust issues, Georgius said if divestitures are required he believes they would be minimal.

When asked about possible future mergers, Georgius said the banking industry is in a consolidating trend and First Union has an "open mind" about "good opportunities at the right price." He said the East Coast of the U.S. is "really our footprint now." First Union's branch system covers Florida to Connecticut. Signet is headquartered in Virginia.
In investment banking, Georgius said First Union intends to grow that business on its own.
